bug_semantics: In Saloon before v4, PendingRequest built its destination with URLHelper::join(connector base URL, request resolveEndpoint()). When resolveEndpoint() returned an attacker-controlled absolute URL, URLHelper::join() returned that URL unchanged, discarding the trusted connector host; the request was then authenticated and could be sent to the attacker host with connector/request headers, cookies, or tokens, enabling SSRF and credential disclosure.
flaw_origin: Commit bef86d8bdec2deec452695cac9517b9ec0b63d7c added the first explicit absolute-endpoint early return to src/Helpers/URLHelper.php: if isValidUrl($endpoint), return $endpoint. Its immediate parent 161aadb2180a61691d7a6345830ca52531507c25 had no such early return and instead retained the base URL, so this atomic human-authored commit first created the host-override mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names Ashley Hood <ashley@opensauce.systems> as both author and committer and contains only the subject 'enhance: UrlHelper join method handle endpoint URL string'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Made-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: The published CVE.org record for CVE-2026-33182 is PUBLISHED and states that prior to 4.0.0 an absolute resolveEndpoint URL replaced the connector base and received attached authentication material; it identifies 4.0.0 as the fix and links the vendor advisory https://github.com/saloonphp/saloon/security/advisories/GHSA-c83f-3xp6-hfcp.

git log --all --reverse -S'static::isValidUrl($endpoint)' -- src/Helpers/URLHelper.php identifies bef86d8bdec2deec452695cac9517b9ec0b63d7c as the first addition of the vulnerable early-return expression; the later matching change is the v4 repair.

git diff bef86d8bdec2deec452695cac9517b9ec0b63d7c^ bef86d8bdec2deec452695cac9517b9ec0b63d7c -- src/Helpers/URLHelper.php shows the atomic addition `if (static::isValidUrl($endpoint)) { return $endpoint; }`; git show of parent 161aadb2180a61691d7a6345830ca52531507c25 confirms that early return is absent and the parent joins the base and endpoint.

At v3.15.0, src/Http/PendingRequest.php assigns URLHelper::join(resolveBaseUrl(), resolveEndpoint()) to the destination, then resolves the authenticator and runs MergeRequestProperties and AuthenticatePendingRequest, closing the absolute-endpoint-to-authenticated-request path.

git tag containment shows the BIC is absent from v1.5.1, first contained in v1.5.2, and contained in v3.15.0; this also shows the advisory's unbounded '< 4.0.0' range is broader than the locally proven introduction boundary, while the real vulnerable lifecycle from v1.5.2 through v3.15.0 remains established.

Direct repair d418356b6257a847f92a0bfa0c2d48bb379c731d changes URLHelper::join() to throw InvalidArgumentException when the connector base is nonempty and the endpoint is absolute, and adds a regression test reproducing an attacker absolute endpoint; its parent still returns the absolute endpoint.

Commit 1307b1d72cacdd2c9c20978cdf7a0b720b4bf3bb adds the documented per-connector/per-request/OAuth allowBaseUrlOverride opt-in while preserving rejection by default; v4.0.0 resolves exactly to this commit, contains d418356b6257a847f92a0bfa0c2d48bb379c731d, and v3.15.0 does not contain the direct fix.

git cat-file commit bef86d8bdec2deec452695cac9517b9ec0b63d7c verifies a single parent, Ashley Hood as author and committer, and no trailers or AI marker. The later v4 carrier 1307b1d72cacdd2c9c20978cdf7a0b720b4bf3bb says 'Made-with: Cursor', but protocol attributes AI only from the BIC and does not transfer a fix marker backward.
reasoning: The advisory mechanism is present in the source lifecycle: the BIC made any syntactically valid absolute request endpoint replace the trusted base; PendingRequest subsequently applied request properties and authentication to that destination. The immediate parent lacks the decisive early return, and the bounded -S history finds no earlier writer of it, so bef86d8bdec2deec452695cac9517b9ec0b63d7c is the smallest public BIC rather than a move, release carrier, fix, or squash aggregate. Tag topology places it in v1.5.2 and later v3 releases, while the direct rejection d418356b6257a847f92a0bfa0c2d48bb379c731d is absent from v3.15.0 and included in v4.0.0; the v4 tag commit 1307b1d72cacdd2c9c20978cdf7a0b720b4bf3bb completes the explicit trusted opt-in design described by the advisory. The BIC commit object has human author/committer identity and no AI marker. The Cursor marker exists only on the later v4 carrier/follow-up, so under BIC-only attribution the real vulnerability is NOT_AI.
